title: A Measure-Theoretic Formulation of Behavioral Systems
summary: In Willems' behavioral systems theory, a dynamical system is identified with the set of all trajectories compatible with its laws of motion. In the linear time-invariant setting this trajectory set is a linear subspace, and its algebraic structure underpins the Fundamental Lemma: a single persistently exciting data trajectory generates the entire finite-horizon behavior. For nonlinear or stochastic systems, however, the admissible trajectory set is generally nonconvex, obstructing direct optimization over the behavior.
